steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Combine the graham cracker crumbs, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl; add the egg, vanilla, and chocolate-hazelnut spread and mix by hand until well blended. Form the mixture into 1 1/2-inch balls and place on a baking sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake in the preheated oven until crispy on the outside, 8 to 10 minutes. Allow to rest on cookie sheet a few minutes before moving to a wire rack to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate-Hazelnut Spread Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These delicious, rich chocolate-hazelnut cookies are crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside.

review.reviewBody:
These are great! I had no problem with them flattening out, I baked them for 8 minutes, left them on the pan for 2 then set them on plates. I suggest storing them with apple slices so they don't dry out.

1 package of Graham Crackers makes about 1 1/2 cups, so I used all of those and added half a cup of Nutella. I also added a Tbsp of cinnamon which REALLY helped draw out the nutty flavor. Even with the addition of ingredients I only got 24 small cookies but they were perfectly delicious!

In the future I'll use 2 cups of Nutella and add some chopped hazelnuts and chocolate chips to the mix! Thanks for the yummy dish!

Followed the basic recipe. I then divided dough in thirds to try different mix-ins. The first one I added 1/2 tsp. cinnamon & 1/4 c. Kraft Caramel Bits. This tasted like snickerdoodles & was good! The next third I added 1/4 c. peanut butter chips & was very good if you like Reese's peanut butter cups. The last third I added about 1/4 c. Nestle Mini Chocolate Chips. If you like double chocolate it was DELICIOUS!! Crispy on outside yet chewy inside. Baked a bit longer than the original as I made the cookies larger and I actually chilled the cookie balls on the parchment lined cookie sheet for an hour before baking. Just keep a watch as to not overcook them. Definitely a keeper & will add to my recipe box. Great way to use up Nutella.

Cookies turned out delicious!
I used 1/4 Egg Beaters instead of egg, since that is what I had available. 
I was concerned that I'd lose too much Nutella in the transfer if a I measured; so, I used a full 13 oz. jar. 
After reading the reviews recommending adding cinnamon, I decided to add a tablespoon of cinnamon. 
Finally, I added a cup of Reese's Peanut Butter Chips. 
I rolled the mix into balls and flattened slightly. I cooked them for 10 minutes, since my oven tends to cook on the slower side. Perfect amount of spread. Great texture. I will make this recipe of many special occasions in the future!!! Thanks for sharing it!!!

DOUBLED THE RECIPE & SOO HAPPY!! DELICIOUS!!! This is an AWESOME recipe to make with kids :) We didn't have any vanilla but they were still soft and chewy :) We also rolled a tray full in cinnamon and sugar and another tray full in icing sugar, a very nice change and the kids couldn't be happier :) :)

Mmm, these were delightful! Be sure not to overbake, I think that's why others had problems with too much spreading. I made sure not to flatten the balls at all and baked them for 7 minutes and immediately transferred to a wire rack for cooling and they were perfect. I made mine with chocolate Teddy Grahams crumbs because that's what was in the pantry. They were a huge hit!
I only used half a cup of Nutella and I still find it too sweet! But my family loved it. Thank you for posting this!
Chewy with a nice crisp outside. I let dough sit in the bowl for 10 minutes at room temperature to firm up before shaping into balls.

These were easy to make and not too sweet. My teen without the sweet-tooth really liked them. I used a silpat on a noninsulated cookie sheet and there was no spread as long as I kept the cook time to about 7 1/2 minutes.

My husband recently discovered Nutella and has been bugging me ever since to make cookies with it. This recipe was PERFECT! So simple! All I had on hand were cinnamon graham crackers and it was delicious. I will definitely be making these again.
Make sure to use Nutella, nothing else. I tried it with a Dutch chocolate hazelnut spread... the cookies didn't taste bad or anything but they were very odd. Tried again with Nutella, perfect.
This is literally the best cookie recipe I've ever had- my roommates agree! I didn't have graham crackers so I used crushed up vanilla wafers. Delicious!
I made these yesterday. They were so good that I made another batch. They are very tasty and light. Will definitely make them again.

Made as per recipe. Dough is very sticky. Baked up very thin and flat. Almost impossible to remove from tray no matter how quickly or not (I used parchment). Finished cookie was thin and crumbly, not chewy. Did not taste like Nutella. I will not make again.

You may wonder how something with so few ingredients (no flour?) could work, but these were exceptional! I made no substitutions and I am at 7300 ft. Elevation....cooked for 7 minutes and allowed them to sit on Silpat for about two minutes. Absolutely mouth-watering, chocolate-y deliciousness! Thanks for the recipe!

It didn't have a good taste .Didn't really taste the nutella. I tasted the graham cracker crumbs. At 8 mins, they were not crispy. After 5 more minutes, the bottoms were overdone. I would not make this again.
Love this recipe! The graham crackers and hazelnutspread made me think s'mores so I actually added bits of marshmallows! Definitely saving this!
I didnt like them at all !!
So easy and everyone loved them! I made a double batch.
I was a bit skeptical when I read the ingredients, but these cookies are fantastic! Simple, easy and delicious!
would recommend adding walnuts to it. Otherwise, delicious
